title: [EXCLUDED] Weak law of large numbers for first-passage percolation times on arbitrary weighted graphs
statement: Conjecture 1. With arbitrary rates (nu_{ij}), if max{xi_{ab} : (a,b) edge in pi_{ij}} / E T^fpp_{ij} ->_p 0 (7.5) then (7.4) holds. [Same page: (7.4) is T^fpp_{ij} / E T^fpp_{ij} ->_p 1; 'We work in the FPP model, writing xi_{ab} for the time to traverse edge (a,b)' (independent Exponential(nu_{ab}) times); pi_{ij} is the random percolation path attaining T^fpp_{ij}; 'It is intuitively clear (and not hard to prove) that condition (7.5) is necessary.' 'Everything depends on n (not written) and limits are as n -> infinity.']
status_search: Dedup: no FPP weak-law rows in intakes A-E (the fpp_survey_2015 rows in the Codex tree are lattice questions: time constant, geodesics, coalescence). Resolved by the source's author: Aldous, 'Weak concentration for first passage percolation times on graphs and general increasing set-valued processes' (arXiv 1604.06418, 2016; the PDF was fetched and read this session). Its text: 'Here is our main result (conjectured in [2] sec. 7.4)', with [2] = 'David Aldous. Interacting particle systems as stochastic social dynamics. Bernoulli, 19(4):1122-1149, 2013', i.e. this source. Theorem 8 there: 'There exist functions psi^+ and psi^-: (0,1] -> (0, infinity) such that psi^+(delta) -> 0 as delta -> 0, and psi^-(delta) > 0 for all delta > 0, and such that, for all finite connected edge-weighted graphs and all vertex pairs (v', v''), psi^-(||Xi(v',v'')/EX(v',v'')||_0) <= s.d.(X(v',v''))/EX(v',v'') <= psi^+(||Xi(v',v'')/EX(v',v'')||_0). In words, X/EX has small spread if and only if Xi/EX is small.' Here ||V||_0 := inf{delta : P(|V| > delta) <= delta} and Xi is 'the maximum edge-traversal time in this minimal-time path'. Matching: the conjecture's hypothesis (7.5) is ||Xi/EX||_0 -> 0, the upper bound gives s.d.(X)/EX -> 0, and Chebyshev gives X/EX ->_p 1, which is (7.4); the lower bound is the source's 'necessary' remark. Section numbering: the source's conjecture sits in its Section 7.2 in the arXiv version read here; Aldous 2016 cites 'sec. 7.4', presumably the journal numbering.
resolved_by: Aldous, arXiv 1604.06418 (2016), Theorem 8, quoted in status_search: psi^-(||Xi/EX||_0) <= s.d.(X)/EX <= psi^+(||Xi/EX||_0) with psi^+(delta) -> 0 as delta -> 0, for all finite connected edge-weighted graphs with independent Exponential edge times of arbitrary rates; the paper states it is the result 'conjectured in [2] sec. 7.4' with [2] this source. Hypothesis (7.5) = ||Xi/EX||_0 -> 0; conclusion (7.4) follows from the upper bound by Chebyshev.

title: Is the sandpile aggregate on a background of holes a regular (4H+12)-gon?
statement: Question 6.2. In Z^2, is the limiting shape of S_{n,H} as n -> infinity a regular (4H+12)-gon? [Same page: 'Simulations indicate that for general H >= -2, the limiting shape of S_{n,H} in Z^2 may be a polygon with 4H + 12 sides.' 'Simulations indicate a regular (4H + 12)-gon with some rounding at the corners; it remains unclear if the rounded portions of the boundary become negligible in the limit. Even if the limiting shape is not a polygon, it would still be very interesting to establish the weaker statement that it has the dihedral symmetry D_{4H+12}.' Figure 11: square, octagon and dodecagon for H = -2, -1, 0.] [Setting, Section 6, PDF p. 29: 'Fey-den Boer and Redig [FR07] consider aggregation in the sandpile model on Z^d. In their setup, the underlying graph for the chip-firing game is the infinite undirected d-dimensional cubic lattice Z^d. Start with each site containing h <= 2d - 2 chips. Here h may be even be taken negative, corresponding to starting with a hole of depth H = -h at each lattice site; that is, each site absorbs the first H chips it receives, and thereafter fires every time it receives an additional four chips. Now add n chips to the origin and stabilize. Denote by S_{n,H} the set of sites in Z^d which fired in the process of stabilization.' Theorem 6.1 ([FR07]): S_{n,2-2d} is a cube C(r_n) for every n; in Z^2, S_{n,-2} is a square. PDF p. 30: 'even the existence of a limiting shape for S_{n,H} has not been proved in the case H > -2', and as H -> infinity the limiting shape is a ball (Fey-Redig; Theorem 6.3 of Levine-Peres).]
status_search: Dedup: sandpile rows in intakes A-E are C0099 (rotor-router recurrence on Z^2), C0100 (height-fraction statistics in the sandpile scaling limit, Levine-Peres open problem (3)) and the jarai_sandpile_2014 rows of this intake (F0055-F0059: toppling-invariant, infinite-volume dynamics, height correlations, none about the aggregate's shape). STATUS: the existence half is settled for the point source: Pegden-Smart, 'Convergence of the Abelian sandpile' (arXiv 1105.0111, Duke Math. J. 2013), abstract summary read: from n chips at a single location 'the authors employ PDE methods to establish convergence to a distinct limit. They identify this limiting configuration as the Laplacian of a solution to an elliptic obstacle problem.' The abstract summary does not state which backgrounds h (holes H) are covered, and says nothing about the shape being a polygon or having D_{4H+12} symmetry; the WebSearch budget was exhausted before a targeted search on polygonality. Levine-Pegden-Smart ('Apollonian structure in the Abelian sandpile', GAFA 2016, and the Annals paper on integer superharmonic matrices, titles known, not read) describe the set Gamma of allowed Hessians of the limit. Kept: polygonality and the D_{4H+12} symmetry are not claimed anywhere I found.

attempt.method: Use the structure of the scaling limit to test the conjectured symmetry. In the Pegden-Smart limit the rescaled odometer u (number of firings) solves an obstacle problem whose constraint is D^2 u in Gamma-bar, Gamma the set of 'integer superharmonic' 2x2 matrices, and the limiting shape is the support {u > 0}. Along a FLAT piece of the free boundary with outward unit normal nu, u vanishes on the face and grows quadratically inside, so its Hessian there is rank one, A = c nu nu^T, and A must lie on the boundary of Gamma. Hence a regular (4H+12)-gon requires the rank-one matrices c nu_k nu_k^T, nu_k = (cos(2 pi k/(4H+12)), sin(2 pi k/(4H+12))), to be extremal points of Gamma for every k.
attempt.result: For H = -2 (square) the normals are the axes and A = c e_i e_i^T, integer matrices, consistent with Theorem 6.1. For H = -1 (octagon) the normals include (1,1)/sqrt 2 and A = (c/2)[[1,1],[1,1]], again rational, consistent with the octagon in the simulations. For H = 0 (dodecagon) the normals at 30 degrees give A = c [[3/4, sqrt(3)/4],[sqrt(3)/4, 1/4]] with irrational off-diagonal ratio, and for H = 1 (16-gon) tan(22.5 degrees) = sqrt 2 - 1 is irrational as well. The Levine-Pegden-Smart description of Gamma (as far as its title and the summary say: the boundary of Gamma is indexed by an Apollonian circle packing, i.e. by rational data) suggests that the extremal rank-one directions of Gamma are rational directions, which would make an exact flat face with normal at 30 degrees impossible; the shapes for H >= 0 would then be D_4-symmetric near-polygons whose 'faces' at irrational angles are slightly curved (the 'rounding' seen in simulations would not be negligible), while H = -2, -1 could be exact polygons. This is a heuristic prediction, direction 'no' for H >= 0 and 'possibly yes' for H = -1; the D_4 symmetry itself is rigorous (the lattice and the initial condition are D_4-invariant and the limit is unique).
attempt.obstruction: Turning the prediction into a theorem needs (i) Pegden-Smart's convergence for the hole backgrounds H > 0 (their stated setting is n chips at the origin, background range not checked here), (ii) a proof that the free boundary of the obstacle problem is a straight segment exactly where the Hessian is an extremal rank-one element of Gamma and curved otherwise, and (iii) the classification of the rank-one boundary points of Gamma from the Apollonian structure. None of these is done here; (iii) is the concrete question to put to the Levine-Pegden-Smart papers.
attempt.key_identity: A flat face with normal nu forces the odometer's Hessian c nu nu^T onto the boundary of Gamma; a regular (4H+12)-gon needs this at the angles 2 pi k/(4H+12), which are irrational directions as soon as H >= 0.

title: Scaling limit of the identity element of the sandpile group of the square grid
statement: Conjecture 6.4. Let a_n be a sequence of integers such that a_n -> infinity and a_n/n -> 0. For x in [0,1] x [0,1] let f_n(x) = (1/a_n^2) sum_{y in G_n, ||y - nx|| <= a_n} I_n(y). There is a sequence a_n and a function f : [0,1] x [0,1] -> R_{>= 0} which is locally constant almost everywhere, such that f_n -> f at all continuity points of f. [PDF p. 30: 'Let I_n be the identity element of the n x n grid graph G_n with wired boundary; the states I_n for four different values of n are pictured in Figure 4. Comparing the pictures of I_n for different values of n, one is struck by their extreme similarity. In particular, we conjecture that as n -> infinity the pictures converge in the following sense to a limiting picture on the unit square.' PDF p. 31: 'Most intriguing is the apparent fractal structure in the conjectural f.']
status_search: Dedup: C0100 (Levine-Peres open problem (3)) concerns height-fraction statistics of the point-source pile, not the identity element; no other identity-element rows. STATUS: WebSearch 2026-09-09 ('sandpile group identity element square grid scaling limit conjecture'): the search summary asserts that the scaling limit of the identity element on Z^2 'was characterized as a consequence of' the Levine-Pegden-Smart / Pegden-Smart papers (2016, 2017, 2020) but no abstract read this session states that theorem, and the summary is a search-engine paraphrase, not a quotation; 'Scaling limit of the sandpile identity element on the Sierpinski gasket' (arXiv 2308.12183) exists for a different graph. Treat as: plausibly resolved by Pegden-Smart's pattern-stability work, unverified. Kept with that flag; whoever merges should read Pegden-Smart, 'Stability of patterns in the Abelian sandpile' (Ann. Henri Poincare 2020) first.

attempt.method: Reduce the identity to two stabilisations with a constant background, so that the point-source PDE theory applies. With m the maximal stable configuration (every non-sink vertex at degree minus one) the identity of the sandpile group is e = (2m - (2m)^o)^o, where ^o is stabilisation: indeed a := 2m - (2m)^o is nonnegative and equals Delta^T u_1 for the toppling vector u_1 of 2m, so for every recurrent r the configuration r + a is in the same equivalence class as r, its stabilisation is recurrent, and the recurrent representative of a class is unique, hence (r + a)^o = r, i.e. a^o is the identity.
attempt.result: So I_n = (2m - (2m)^o)^o is determined by two odometers: u_1 for the constant configuration 2m = 6 on the interior of the n x n grid with wired (sink) boundary, and u_2 for the configuration a = 2m - (2m)^o = Delta^T u_1 restricted to the grid. In the scaling limit, u_1/n^2 should converge to the solution of the obstacle problem on the unit square with zero boundary values and constraint D^2 u in Gamma-bar plus the 'background 6' condition, which is the Dirichlet-boundary analogue of the Pegden-Smart point-source problem; the height pattern of (2m)^o is then locally constant on the regions where D^2 u_1 is constant (an element of the Apollonian family), which is exactly the block-average statement of the conjecture for the intermediate configuration. Conjecture 6.4 therefore reduces to: (i) Pegden-Smart convergence for a constant background with a Dirichlet boundary instead of a point source, (ii) pattern stability (block averages of the height converge to the pattern densities on each region where the limiting Hessian is constant), and (iii) the same two steps for the second stabilisation, whose input a = Delta^T u_1 is itself locally patterned. The locally-constant-a.e. limit f in the conjecture is then the composition of pattern densities, and the 'fractal' is the Apollonian tiling of the square by regions of constant Hessian.
attempt.obstruction: Steps (i) and (iii) are not covered by the point-source theorem as stated in its abstract (the sink is the boundary, not a point, and the second stabilisation starts from a non-constant configuration); step (ii) is what the 'stability of patterns' paper is about and may already give the full conjecture, which I could not verify this session. Also the conjecture asks for a SINGLE sequence a_n with convergence at continuity points of f; the PDE route gives it for every a_n -> infinity with a_n = o(n) once the pattern densities are well defined.
attempt.key_identity: Identity e = (2m - (2m)^o)^o; each stabilisation is an obstacle problem with Hessian constraint in Gamma, and the identity's picture is the Apollonian region decomposition of the square applied twice.

locator: Conjecture 7.1 (Voiculescu's unification problem), Chapter 7, PDF p. 81
title: Microstates and non-microstates free entropy coincide when the former is finite
statement: Conjecture 7.1: For any tau such that chi(tau) > -infinity, chi(tau) = chi*(tau). [Same page: 'The conjecture (named unification problem by D. Voiculescu [129])'.] [Setting, Chapter 7, PDF pp. 80-81: tau in M(m) is a tracial law of m non-commutative self-adjoint variables; chi(tau) is Voiculescu's microstates free entropy (defined through the volume of sets of m-tuples of N x N Hermitian matrices whose empirical distribution approximates tau); Phi*(tau) = sum_i ||D*_{X_i} 1||^2_{L^2(tau)} is the free Fisher information and chi*(tau) = -(1/2) int_0^1 Phi*(tau_t^b) dt (with tau_t^b the law of (t X_i + sqrt(t(1-t)) S_i), S_i free semicirculars free from X) is the non-microstates free entropy, up to the source's normalisation; Theorem 7.3 ([18], Biane-Capitaine-Guionnet): chi(tau) <= chi*(tau) for every tau. Remark 7.2: 'If the conjecture would hold for any tau in M(m) and not only for tau with finite microstates entropy, it would provide an affirmative answer to Connes question since it is known that if tau is the law of X_1, ..., X_m and S_1, ..., S_m free semicircular variables, free with X_1, ..., X_m then, for any epsilon > 0 the distribution tau_epsilon of (X_1 + epsilon S_1, ..., X_m + epsilon S_m) satisfies chi*(tau_epsilon) > -infinity, and hence the above equality would imply chi(tau_epsilon) > -infinity so that one could find matrices whose empirical distribution approximates tau_epsilon and thus tau since epsilon can be chosen arbitrarily small.']
status_search: Dedup: 'microstates|free entropy' 0 hits across intakes A-E (voiculescu_free_entropy_2002 is an F source with no rows; the Codex tree's aim_free_analysis_2006 has 0 rows). WebSearch 2026-09-09 ('microstates free entropy equals non-microstates ... status'): summary of results found: Biane-Capitaine-Guionnet proved chi <= chi* (the source's Theorem 7.3), Jekel-Pi (2024) extended the inequality to conditional entropies ('An elementary proof of the inequality chi <= chi* for conditional free entropy', arXiv 2305.02574), Dabrowski ('A Laplace principle for Hermitian Brownian motion and free entropy I: the convex functional case', arXiv 1604.06420, 2017) proved chi = chi* for free Gibbs laws with convex potentials under regularity and growth conditions; the general problem is described as open as of 2024. Kept.

attempt.method: Combine the source's own Remark 7.2 with the refutation of the Connes embedding conjecture. Remark 7.2 shows: (strong form: chi = chi* for EVERY tau) implies (every tau in M(m) is a limit of matrix microstates), i.e. Connes' embedding property for all tracial laws of finitely many variables. The Connes embedding conjecture was refuted by Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, Yuen ('MIP* = RE', arXiv 2001.04383, 2020; my knowledge, not re-fetched this session): there is a tracial von Neumann algebra, hence a law tau of finitely many self-adjoint generators, that is not approximable by matrix microstates.
attempt.result: Contrapositive of Remark 7.2: the strong form of the conjecture is FALSE. Explicitly, for a non-embeddable tau and any epsilon > 0, the semicircular perturbation tau_epsilon has chi*(tau_epsilon) > -infinity (the source's Remark 7.2, finite free Fisher information) while chi(tau_epsilon) = -infinity (otherwise tau_epsilon, hence tau, would have microstates). So chi and chi* differ, by an infinite amount, on a non-empty set of laws, and the hypothesis 'chi(tau) > -infinity' in Conjecture 7.1 is not a technicality: it is exactly what excludes the known counterexamples. Conjecture 7.1 as stated survives (the counterexamples have chi = -infinity), and is equivalent to the reverse inequality chi >= chi* on {chi > -infinity}.
attempt.obstruction: For the reverse inequality the only available mechanism is Dabrowski's large-deviation (Laplace principle) argument, which needs a convex potential to control the Hermitian Brownian motion; without convexity there is no known way to produce enough microstates from finite free Fisher information, and the MIP* = RE example shows that finite Fisher information alone never suffices. Since chi <= chi* always, finiteness of chi* is automatic on the conjecture's domain; the issue is laws with microstates but strictly larger chi*, for which no candidate is known.
attempt.key_identity: Remark 7.2 + (Connes embedding is false) => the unrestricted conjecture chi = chi* is false; the stated conjecture is the reverse inequality chi >= chi* on {chi > -infinity}.

locator: Conjecture 5.1 (Zvonkin's genus expansion of the quartic matrix integral), Chapter 5, PDF p. 54
title: [EXCLUDED] Genus expansion of the one-matrix quartic integral counts maps
statement: Conjecture 5.1: [see A. Zvonkin's [136]] For any N in N, any t in R, (1/N^2) log int exp(-N Tr(t A^4 + (1/4) A^2)) dA = sum_{n >= 0} sum_{g >= 0} ((-t)^n / n!) N^{-2g} C(n, g). [PDF p. 55: 'C(n, g) = number of maps of genus g with n vertices of degree 4', maps counted up to homeomorphism; the integral is over N x N Hermitian matrices. PDF p. 56: 'Of course, this derivation is formal and it is not clear at all that such an expansion of the free energy exists. Indeed, the series here might well not be summable (this is clear when t < 0 since the integral diverges).']
status_search: Resolved, and the source says so on the next pages: PDF p. 56: 'In the one matrix case, this result was proved very recently by J. Mc Laughlin et N. Ercolani [46] who have shown that such an expansion is valid by mean of Riemann-Hilbert problems techniques, under natural assumptions over the potential.' Ercolani-McLaughlin, 'Asymptotics of the partition function for random matrices via Riemann-Hilbert techniques, and applications to graphical enumeration' (arXiv math-ph/0211022, IMRN 2003), abstract read verbatim: 'We obtain the first proof of a complete large N expansion for the partition function, for a general class of probability measures on matrices, originally conjectured by Bessis, Itzykson, and Zuber. We prove that the coefficients in the asymptotic expansion are analytic functions of parameters in the original probability measure, and that they are generating functions for the enumeration of labelled maps according to genus and valence.' The quartic potential t x^4 + x^2/4 is the single-monomial case of their class. Read literally ('for any N, any t in R', with an equality sign) the conjecture is not a well-posed statement (the source itself notes divergence for t < 0, and for fixed g the sum over n has finite radius); the meaningful content, the asymptotic expansion in 1/N^2 with map-counting coefficients for small t > 0, is the Ercolani-McLaughlin theorem.
resolved_by: The source's own p. 56 sentence ('In the one matrix case, this result was proved very recently by J. Mc Laughlin et N. Ercolani [46]') plus Ercolani-McLaughlin, IMRN 2003 (arXiv math-ph/0211022): 'the first proof of a complete large N expansion for the partition function ... the coefficients ... are generating functions for the enumeration of labelled maps according to genus and valence'. The one-matrix quartic case stated in the conjecture is inside their class; the literal 'for any N, any t' equality is a formal statement the source itself qualifies.

locator: Section 5.2, PDF p. 14 (the sentence 'recurrence in dimension 2 with d_alpha = 0 remains open')
title: Recurrence of the two-dimensional random walk in Dirichlet environment with zero mean drift
statement: Let us stress that recurrence in dimension 2 with d_alpha = 0 remains open. [Context, PDF pp. 13-14: Theorem 2 (from [35]) gives transience of the RWDE for d >= 3 and every choice of weights, and, in d = 2, the annealed identity P_0(walk hits distance N before returning to 0) equal to the same probability for the simple random walk in the mean environment, whose order is (ln N)^{-1}; 'hence 2D annealed RWDE are strictly less recurrent than the symmetric simple random walk'. The question is whether, for P^(alpha)-almost every environment, the RWDE on Z^2 with d_alpha = 0 returns to 0 infinitely often.] [Setting of the source, Sections 2-5: a random walk in Dirichlet environment (RWDE) on Z^d with weights alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d} > 0 attached to the 2d nearest-neighbour directions e_1, ..., e_{2d} (e_{i+d} = -e_i): at each site the transition probabilities (omega(x, x + e_i))_i are an independent Dirichlet(alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d}) vector; P^(alpha) is the law of the environment, P_0^(alpha) the annealed law of the walk from 0. d_alpha := sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i e_i is the mean drift direction; kappa := 2 sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i - max_{1 <= i <= d} (alpha_i + alpha_{i+d}) (PDF p. 11, (4.3)) is the integrability exponent of the Green function of the strongest finite trap (a pair of neighbours). Theorem 1 (PDF p. 12): if d_alpha . l != 0 the walk is transient in the direction of sign(d_alpha . l) l, and if d_alpha != 0 it has asymptotic direction d_alpha/|d_alpha|, P_0^(alpha)-a.s. Proposition 2 (PDF p. 11): if kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0. Theorem 5 (PDF p. 16): (i) if d >= 3, d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1 then X_n/n -> v != 0; (ii) if d_alpha = 0 or kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0; (iii) if d >= 3, d_alpha . l > 0 and kappa <= 1 then log(X_n . l)/log n -> kappa in probability. (T)^gamma is Sznitman's ballisticity condition (exponential decay, at rate L^gamma, of the annealed probability of exiting a slab of width L on the wrong side).]
status_search: Dedup: 'Dirichlet environment|ballistic' hits are the drewitz_ramirez_rwre_2014 rows C0040-C0046/P0482-P0488 (invariant measure versus ballisticity; transience implies ballisticity for UNIFORMLY elliptic i.i.d. RWRE in d >= 2, C0041; ballisticity under an ellipticity moment condition, C0042; (T) versus (T'), C0046; (P)_M, C0045) and C0134 (excited random walks). Dirichlet environments are not uniformly elliptic and the three statements here are specific to them; none coincides with a listed row. WebSearch budget exhausted before this row; arXiv API search 'ti:"Dirichlet environment" submittedDate 2017-2026' failed (HTTP 429) and could not be repeated in time. My recollection (not verified): no paper proves quenched recurrence of the 2D RWDE with zero mean drift. Kept, flagged as status-checked only through the source (2016) and the reference list of the Codex tree's drewitz_ramirez rows.

attempt.method: Separate annealed from quenched, and identify what a proof needs. The annealed identity of the source (hitting probability of distance N before return equal to that of the simple random walk in the mean environment, order 1/ln N) says the ANNEALED walk is recurrent in the sense that P_0(return) = 1; but annealed recurrence is a statement about the mixture and does not give quenched recurrence: by the directional 0-1 laws of the source (Theorem 1 (i) for d_alpha = 0 gives liminf X_n . l = -infinity < limsup = +infinity for every l, i.e. the walk oscillates in every direction), the quenched event {return to 0 infinitely often} has P^(alpha)-probability 0 or 1 (0-1 law of Section 5.3 / Kalikow-type argument, valid as the environment is i.i.d.), so the question is which.
attempt.result: Two partial reductions. (1) Quenched recurrence in d = 2 with d_alpha = 0 would follow from an absolutely continuous invariant measure for the environment seen from the particle together with a quenched invariance principle with non-degenerate covariance: for balanced environments in d = 2 this is how Lawler's argument runs... no, an invariance principle alone is compatible with transience; what gives recurrence in d = 2 is the combination of the invariant measure (which makes the walk 'stationary' in a suitable sense) with a Nash-Williams / Kesten type estimate on the number of visits, which for reversible walks is available and for RWDE is not. So reduction (1) is only to the existence of the invariant measure plus a genuinely new non-reversible recurrence criterion. (2) The time-reversal property of Dirichlet environments (the reversed environment is again Dirichlet with reversed weights, Sabot-Tournier 2011) gives, for d_alpha = 0, that the walk and its time-reversal have the same annealed law of the environment; a quenched recurrence proof could try to use this symmetry to compare the walk to its reversal on the loops around 0 (a loop-based Kalikow argument), which I could not complete.
attempt.obstruction: Every known recurrence proof in d = 2 (reversible walks, balanced walks) uses either an electrical network or an exact martingale structure; RWDE with d_alpha = 0 has neither: the environment is non-reversible and the quenched walk has a random, non-zero local drift with heavy-tailed (Beta) transition probabilities, so traps of finite size have infinite expected exit time when kappa <= 1 (Proposition 2), and the quenched walk spends most of its time in such traps; recurrence must be proved through the trap structure, which is where the 2D case differs from d >= 3 (Theorem 2's transience proof uses transience of the mean-environment walk, unavailable in d = 2).
attempt.key_identity: Annealed: P_0(hit distance N before return) has the same order (ln N)^{-1} as the simple random walk in the mean environment; the open question is the quenched 0-1 event 'return to 0 infinitely often'.

locator: Section 4, PDF p. 11 (the sentence following Proposition 2)
title: Sharpness of kappa <= 1 for non-ballisticity of the Dirichlet walk in dimension two

We see that it is not true for non uniformly elliptic environment, in particular for Dirichlet environment. Nevertheless, the previous theorem shows that with a slightly different notion of ballisticity, which involves the parameter kappa which is a function of the environment, directional transience implies ballisticity. It hence gives in dimension d >= 3 for Dirichlet environments an answer to the conjecture. It is expected that the same is true in dimension d = 2, but we are still far for a proof of that.'] [Setting of the source, Sections 2-5: a random walk in Dirichlet environment (RWDE) on Z^d with weights alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d} > 0 attached to the 2d nearest-neighbour directions e_1, ..., e_{2d} (e_{i+d} = -e_i): at each site the transition probabilities (omega(x, x + e_i))_i are an independent Dirichlet(alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d}) vector; P^(alpha) is the law of the environment, P_0^(alpha) the annealed law of the walk from 0. d_alpha := sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i e_i is the mean drift direction; kappa := 2 sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i - max_{1 <= i <= d} (alpha_i + alpha_{i+d}) (PDF p. 11, (4.3)) is the integrability exponent of the Green function of the strongest finite trap (a pair of neighbours). Theorem 1 (PDF p. 12): if d_alpha . l != 0 the walk is transient in the direction of sign(d_alpha . l) l, and if d_alpha != 0 it has asymptotic direction d_alpha/|d_alpha|, P_0^(alpha)-a.s. Proposition 2 (PDF p. 11): if kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0. Theorem 5 (PDF p. 16): (i) if d >= 3, d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1 then X_n/n -> v != 0; (ii) if d_alpha = 0 or kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0; (iii) if d >= 3, d_alpha . l > 0 and kappa <= 1 then log(X_n . l)/log n -> kappa in probability. attempt.method: Identify the missing ingredient by comparing with the d >= 3 proof. Theorem 5 (i) is, per the source's Remark 6, 'a consequence of the existence of an absolutely continuous invariant measure' for the environment seen from the particle (Theorem 3/4: exists in d >= 3 when kappa > 1, with density in L^p for p < kappa). Given such a measure Q, the law of large numbers with non-zero speed follows from the ergodic theorem applied to the local drift, plus the directional transience of Theorem 1 to rule out v = 0. So the conjecture in d = 2 reduces to: for d = 2, d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1, does the environment seen from the particle admit an invariant probability measure absolutely continuous with respect to P^(alpha)?
attempt.result: The construction of Q in d >= 3 (Sabot 2013, the source's [36]) goes through the time-reversal property and transience of the mean-environment simple random walk on Z^d, d >= 3, used to show that the total weight of paths returning to a finite box is finite. In d = 2 with d_alpha != 0 the mean-environment walk is a walk with drift, which is transient too, so the transience input is available; what changes is the entropy/trap bookkeeping: the density of Q is built from Green functions of finite boxes whose integrability exponent is kappa_Lambda (Theorem 4's formula, the strongest finite trap containing 0 and touching the box boundary), and in d = 2 the boundary of a box of radius r has order r sites while the box has r^2, so the traps 'touching the boundary' are a positive fraction of all pairs and the L^p bound on the density may fail even though kappa > 1. Hence the conjecture is equivalent (via the source's own route) to an L^1 bound on the Radon-Nikodym density of the environment seen from the particle in d = 2, and the difficulty is the boundary-trap count, not the transience.
attempt.obstruction: I could not decide whether the L^1 bound holds in d = 2; the alternative route through regeneration times (Corollary 2: finite s-moments for s < kappa under condition (6.1) and (T)^gamma) would give ballisticity from kappa > 1 directly, but requires (T)^gamma, which is the content of F0137 and is itself open in this generality. Numerically, simulating the RWDE on Z^2 with alpha = (2, 1, 1.2, 1.2) (kappa = 2 (5.4) - max(3, 2.4) = 7.8 > 1, d_alpha = (1, 0)) and measuring X_n/n at n = 10^5, 10^6 would show whether the speed stabilises at a positive value, an easy check not done here.
attempt.key_identity: Ballisticity in d >= 3 = (invariant measure Q << P, density in L^p, p < kappa) + ergodic theorem; in d = 2 the density bound must survive a boundary of size r rather than r^{d-1} << r^d.

locator: Section 6.1, PDF p. 19 (the sentence following Corollary 2)
title: Sznitman's condition (T)^gamma holds for every directionally transient Dirichlet walk
statement: It is expected that this condition is not optimal, and we conjecture that at least (T)^gamma is satisfied when d_alpha != 0, hence that renewal times have finite s-moments for s < kappa when the RWDE is directionally transient, i.e. when d_alpha != 0. [Context, PDF pp. 18-19: Corollary 2: 'Assume that d >= 2 and that d_alpha . l > 0 for some direction l. Assume that the condition (6.1) is satisfied, and denote (tau_k)_{k >= 1} the renewal times in the direction l. Then E_0[tau_1^s] < infinity if and only if s < kappa.' Condition (6.1) is the source's sufficient condition for (T)^gamma (a lower bound on the weights in a half space, from Bouchet-Ramirez-Sabot and Fribergh-Kious); 'this condition' in the conjecture is (6.1).] [Setting of the source, Sections 2-5: a random walk in Dirichlet environment (RWDE) on Z^d with weights alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d} > 0 attached to the 2d nearest-neighbour directions e_1, ..., e_{2d} (e_{i+d} = -e_i): at each site the transition probabilities (omega(x, x + e_i))_i are an independent Dirichlet(alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2d}) vector; P^(alpha) is the law of the environment, P_0^(alpha) the annealed law of the walk from 0. d_alpha := sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i e_i is the mean drift direction; kappa := 2 sum_{i=1}^{2d} alpha_i - max_{1 <= i <= d} (alpha_i + alpha_{i+d}) (PDF p. 11, (4.3)) is the integrability exponent of the Green function of the strongest finite trap (a pair of neighbours). Theorem 1 (PDF p. 12): if d_alpha . l != 0 the walk is transient in the direction of sign(d_alpha . l) l, and if d_alpha != 0 it has asymptotic direction d_alpha/|d_alpha|, P_0^(alpha)-a.s. Proposition 2 (PDF p. 11): if kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0. Theorem 5 (PDF p. 16): (i) if d >= 3, d_alpha != 0 and kappa > 1 then X_n/n -> v != 0; (ii) if d_alpha = 0 or kappa <= 1 then X_n/n -> 0; (iii) if d >= 3, d_alpha . l > 0 and kappa <= 1 then log(X_n . l)/log n -> kappa in probability. (T)^gamma is Sznitman's ballisticity condition (exponential decay, at rate L^gamma, of the annealed probability of exiting a slab of width L on the wrong side).]

attempt.method: Reduce (T)^gamma for RWDE to a statement about the annealed exit distribution, using the Polya-urn representation. In a Dirichlet environment the annealed walk is a directed-edge-reinforced random walk (each exit from x along e_i is chosen with probability proportional to alpha_i plus the number of previous exits along that edge), so the annealed probability of exiting a slab {0 <= x . l <= L} on the wrong side is the probability that this reinforced walk backtracks by L. (T)^gamma asks that this probability decays like exp(-c L^gamma) for the slab of width L (with the width in the other directions polynomial in L).
attempt.result: Comparison with the mean environment: without reinforcement the walk has drift d_alpha/|alpha| and the backtracking probability decays exponentially in L (a large deviation of a drifted walk), which is (T)^1. Reinforcement only ever increases the probability of repeating a previous step, so along a backtracking path the reinforcement favours the very moves the path has already made in the backward direction; the question is whether this feedback can raise the backtracking probability from exp(-cL) to a stretched-exponential or polynomial in L. The finite-trap analysis (Section 4) shows the walk can be held for a long TIME in a pair of sites (exit-time tail with exponent kappa), but holding time does not create backtracking DISTANCE: a trap of diameter 1 delays the walk without moving it back. Since the integrability exponent of traps of any finite size is still kappa (Proposition 1: the strongest traps are pairs), no finite structure produces a long backward excursion cheaply, and the only way to backtrack by L is a path of length at least L against the drift, each step of which pays a fixed factor in the annealed (urn) probability once the relevant edges have been used O(1) times. This gives (T)^gamma at least for backtracking paths that do not revisit sites often; the whole problem is the paths that revisit the same sites many times (where reinforcement is strong) while still progressing backward, i.e. 'reinforced tunnels'.
attempt.obstruction: Bounding the contribution of reinforced tunnels needs a decomposition of the backtracking event by the number of distinct sites visited, and for paths that visit few sites the urn weights grow linearly with the visits, so the probability cost per backward step decays to zero along the path; whether the sum over tunnel shapes still gives exp(-c L^gamma) is exactly the (T)^gamma question and I could not settle it. The source's condition (6.1) presumably kills the tunnels by a weight lower bound; the conjecture says they are harmless without it.
attempt.key_identity: Annealed RWDE = directed-edge-reinforced walk with initial weights alpha; (T)^gamma is a large deviation for backtracking of that reinforced walk, and finite traps cost time, not distance.

title: Two-point Airy_2 law of the narrow-wedge KPZ equation at large time
statement: Conjecture. For every w in R it holds that lim_{t -> infinity} P(lambda_t^{-1/3} xi(0, t) <= s_1, lambda_t^{-1/3} xi(2 lambda_t^2 w, t) <= s_2) = det(1 - K^{(2)}_{s_1, s_2; w}), (2.9) where K^{(2)}_{s_1,s_2;w} is the extended Airy kernel. The determinant needs some explanations. K^{(2)} acts on L^2(R x {1,2}) and is given by K^{(2)}_{s_1,s_2;w} = diag(P_{s_1}, P_{s_2}) [[K_Ai, -e^{-|w| H}(1 - K_Ai)], [e^{|w| H} K_Ai, K_Ai]] (2.10). [Context, PDF pp. 9-10: h(x, t) is the Cole-Hopf solution of the KPZ equation with sharp wedge initial data; xi(x, t) = h(x, t) + x^2/(2t) + t/24 (2.5) is the deviation from the parabola; lambda_t = (t/2)^{1/3}; (2.8): lim P(lambda_t^{-1} xi(0, t) <= s) = det(1 - P_s K_Ai P_s) (GUE Tracy-Widom); 'The obvious next step would be to consider the joint distribution of xi(0, t), xi(x, t). No closed expression as in (2.6) is available. But, based on universality, the long time behavior is conjectured with a high level of confidence.' Transcription note: the extracted text of (2.9) and of the sentence before it reads lambda_t^{-1/3}, while (2.8) reads lambda_t^{-1}; since lambda_t = (t/2)^{1/3} already carries the 1/3, the intended normalisation is lambda_t^{-1} xi as in (2.8), and the attempt uses that. H is the Airy Hamiltonian.]
status_search: Dedup: the KPZ rows in intakes A-E (corwin_kpz_2012, aim_kpz_2025, owr_2024_51, ferrari_spohn_growth_2010 in this intake) are about other objects (universality of exponents, weak-noise, half-space, polymer questions); no row states the narrow-wedge two-point law. STATUS, likely resolved but only in preprints: the conjecture follows from (a) convergence of the narrow-wedge KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point / Airy_2 process at one time under the 1:2:3 scaling and (b) the extended-Airy-kernel formula for the finite-dimensional distributions of the Airy_2 process (Prahofer-Spohn 2002; recovered as a special case in Matetski-Quastel-Remenik, 'The KPZ fixed point', arXiv 1701.00018, Acta Math. 2021, abstract read: their formula 'recovers known solutions including the Airy_1 and Airy_2 processes'). For (a): Quastel-Sarkar, 'Convergence of exclusion processes and the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point' (arXiv 2008.06584; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 36 (2023)) - the arXiv abstract page read this session says the paper 'has been withdrawn by Jeremy Quastel' (v3 5 Oct 2020 and v7 7 May 2025 are withdrawal notices) with the comment 'A shift is missing in (5.14). This ruins the averaging argument in the lines which follow ... The main estimates (6.1) and (6.2) (and therefore the main results) should be true, but presently there is a gap in the proof'. Virag, 'The heat and the landscape I' (arXiv 2008.07241, Aug 2020, no journal reference on its page), abstract: convergence of 'the O'Connell-Yor polymer and the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point'. Wu, 'The KPZ equation and the directed landscape' (arXiv 2301.00547, v3 April 2025, no journal reference on its page), abstract read verbatim: 'This paper proves the convergence of the narrow wedge solutions of the KPZ equation to the Airy sheet and the directed landscape in the locally uniform topology ... We also give an independent proof for the convergence of the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point for general initial conditions in the locally uniform topology.' So two independent preprints claim (a) and the published proof has a declared gap. Following the campaign's admit-when-in-doubt rule (the E-ledger's E0050 precedent) the row is ADMITTED with this record; it should be re-classified as resolved once Wu's or Virag's paper is refereed and published.

attempt.method: Write out the dependency chain and check the scalings so that the conjecture is exactly the one-time, two-point marginal of the narrow-wedge KPZ fixed point. With lambda_t = (t/2)^{1/3}, the 1:2:3 scaling of the narrow-wedge Cole-Hopf solution reads h(x, t) = -x^2/(2t) - t/24 + lambda_t A_2(x/(2 lambda_t^2)) + o(lambda_t) in law, where the KPZ fixed point from the narrow wedge at time 1 is A_2(y) - y^2 with A_2 the Airy_2 process, and the parabola -y^2 corresponds to -x^2/(2t) after the substitution x = 2 lambda_t^2 y: indeed (2 lambda_t^2 y)^2/(2t) = 2 lambda_t^4 y^2/t = 2 (t/2)^{4/3} y^2/t = 2^{-1/3} t^{1/3} y^2 = lambda_t y^2. So xi(2 lambda_t^2 w, t)/lambda_t -> A_2(w) and xi(0,t)/lambda_t -> A_2(0), with the parabola exactly absorbed by (2.5); the joint law of (A_2(0), A_2(w)) is det(1 - K^{(2)}) with the extended Airy kernel in the form (2.10) (Prahofer-Spohn's two-point formula, with the e^{+-|w| H} conjugation by the Airy Hamiltonian H = -d^2/dx^2 + x). So (2.9) is precisely 'one-time convergence of the narrow-wedge KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point, evaluated at two space points', with all constants matching the source's (2.5) and (2.8).
attempt.result: The conjecture is therefore equivalent to statement (a) of the status record specialised to two points at one time, and is settled if either Wu 2023 or Virag 2020 is correct; nothing further is proved here. One independent consistency check: at w = 0 the kernel K^{(2)} reduces to the block matrix with K_Ai on the diagonal and (P_{s_1}, P_{s_2}) projections, so (2.9) gives P(A_2(0) <= min(s_1, s_2)) = F_GUE(min(s_1, s_2)), which is (2.8): the conjecture is consistent with the proved one-point law. As |w| -> infinity the off-diagonal blocks decay (e^{-|w|H} on the range of K_Ai... contracts) and (2.9) tends to F_GUE(s_1) F_GUE(s_2), the expected asymptotic independence stated in the source.
attempt.obstruction: The honest gap is exactly the one the withdrawn paper names: the tightness/identification of the limit of the KPZ equation under the 1:2:3 scaling needs a control of the KPZ line ensemble (or of the exclusion-process comparison) that is uniform in space, and the two preprints supply it by different routes (Baik-Ben Arous-Peche statistics; Airy line ensemble convergence). I did not read either proof; the row is a pointer, not a result.
attempt.key_identity: (2 lambda_t^2 w)^2/(2t) = lambda_t w^2, so (2.5)'s parabola is the KPZ fixed point's -w^2 and (2.9) is the two-point Airy_2 law under the 1:2:3 scaling with lambda_t = (t/2)^{1/3}.

locator: Section 4.3, PDF p. 14 (the sentence 'It remains an open question to construct QLE(gamma^2, eta) for the full range of parameter values')
title: Construction of quantum Loewner evolution for all parameters (gamma^2, eta)
statement: It remains an open question to construct QLE(gamma^2, eta) for the full range of parameter values. [Context, Section 4.3, PDF pp. 13-14: 'The process QLE(8/3, 0) described in Section 4.2 is a part of a general family of growth processes which are the conjectural scaling limits of a family of growth models on random surfaces'; 'The dielectric breakdown model (DBM) [73] with parameter eta is a family of models which interpolate between the Eden model and diffusion limited aggregation (DLA). If nu_HARM (resp. nu_LEN) denotes the natural harmonic (resp. length) measure on the underlying surface, then microscopic particles are added according to the measure (d nu_HARM / d nu_LEN)^eta d nu_LEN. In particular, eta = 0 corresponds to the Eden model and eta = 1 corresponds to DLA. One can apply the tip-rerandomization procedure to SLE_kappa or SLE_kappa' coupled with gamma-LQG for other values of gamma, kappa' and eta provided kappa = gamma^2 and kappa' = 16/gamma^2. The resulting process, which is called QLE(gamma^2, eta) and is defined and analyzed in [70], is the conjectural scaling limit of eta-DBM on a gamma-LQG surface where eta = 3 gamma^2/16 - 1/2 or eta = 3/gamma^2 - 1/2. (The parameter gamma determines the type of LQG surface on which the process grows and the value of eta determines the manner in which it grows.) Special parameter values include QLE(8/3, 0) and QLE(2, 1), the latter being the conjectural scaling limit of DLA on a tree-weighted random planar map.' Figure 2 (right) plots the (gamma^2, eta) values for which QLE is constructed in [70]: the two curves above, through (2, 1), (8/3, 0), (4, 1/4).]
status_search: Dedup: 'Loewner evolution|QLE' 0 hits across intakes A-E; the LQG rows in the union (ddg_lqg_metric_intro_2021, gwynne_random_surfaces_2020, ghs_mating_trees_survey_2019, sheffield_random_surface_2022, legall) concern the metric, mating of trees and planar-map convergence, not QLE. STATUS: arXiv API search 'ti:"quantum Loewner evolution"' (2026-09-09) returned Miller-Sheffield, 'Quantum Loewner evolution' (arXiv 1312.5745, the source's [70]) and Ang-Mithal, 'Quantum Loewner evolution in quantum natural time: phases and Markov properties' (arXiv 2605.03385, May 2026), abstract read verbatim: 'Their construction applies to pairs (gamma^2, eta) lying on a curve in parameter space ... In this paper we construct quantum natural time QLE(gamma^2, eta) for a different but overlapping subset of the same parameter curve.' So as of May 2026 the construction is still confined to the special curves; the full range remains open. Kept.

attempt.method: Pin down why the construction is restricted to the curves eta = 3 gamma^2/16 - 1/2 and eta = 3/gamma^2 - 1/2, and what a general construction would have to replace. The Miller-Sheffield construction runs a radial SLE_kappa (kappa = gamma^2) or SLE_kappa' on a gamma-LQG surface and periodically re-randomises the tip according to the quantum boundary length measure raised to a power; the process is a QLE only if the re-randomised law is stationary, and stationarity of the (surface, tip) pair is an exact identity that holds because the SLE/LQG coupling (the quantum zipper) makes the boundary measure conformally covariant with a specific exponent. Writing the tip re-randomisation density as (harmonic measure / boundary length)^eta, the exponent eta for which the zipper symmetry closes is forced by the boundary scaling exponent of gamma-LQG and by the SLE parameter: eta = 3 gamma^2/16 - 1/2 for kappa = gamma^2 < 4 and eta = 3/gamma^2 - 1/2 for kappa' = 16/gamma^2 > 4 (these are the two curves; check: gamma^2 = 8/3 gives eta = 1/2 - 1/2 = 0 on the first curve, gamma^2 = 2 gives eta = 3/2 - 1/2 = 1 on the second, matching QLE(8/3, 0) and QLE(2, 1)).
attempt.result: So the restriction is not technical: off the two curves there is no SLE-based process whose tip re-randomisation is stationary, and a general QLE(gamma^2, eta) has to be defined as a limit of discretisations (delta-step reshuffled SLE with a non-stationary tilt) with no exact solvability to lean on. This reduces the open question to two sub-problems: (1) tightness of the delta-reshuffled processes off the curves (the boundary-length process is then not a stable Levy process but a tilted one, and the tilt e^{(eta - eta_c(gamma)) log(harmonic/length)} has to be controlled through the multifractal spectrum of SLE harmonic measure, whose exponents are known); (2) a characterisation of the limit (a Markov property for the unexplored surface, which Ang-Mithal 2026 establish on their curve for the quantum-natural-time variant, plus scale invariance) strong enough to make the limit unique. The multifractal spectrum of harmonic measure on SLE gives that the tilt has finite moments in a window of eta around eta_c(gamma) of width determined by the spectrum, which is a concrete candidate for the range where sub-problem (1) is tractable: |eta - eta_c(gamma)| small.
attempt.obstruction: Sub-problem (2) is the real one: without stationarity there is no exact description of the limit, and uniqueness would have to come from a general characterisation of growth processes on LQG surfaces by their Markov property and scaling, which does not exist (the analogous characterisation of SLE by domain Markov and conformal invariance has no LQG-growth counterpart). I did not attempt the tilt estimates.
attempt.key_identity: Stationarity of the tip re-randomisation forces eta = 3 gamma^2/16 - 1/2 (kappa = gamma^2 < 4) or eta = 3/gamma^2 - 1/2 (kappa' = 16/gamma^2 > 4); off these curves QLE must be built as a limit of tilted, non-stationary reshufflings.

locator: Chapter 10 (open problems), second bullet 'Partial recovery', PDF p. 116
title: [EXCLUDED] Existence of the limit of the mutual information per vertex in the sparse assortative two-community SBM
statement: Partial recovery. What is the fundamental tradeoff between the SNR and the distortion (MMSE, agreement or mutual information) for partial recovery and arbitrary constant degrees? As a preliminary result, one may attempt to show that I(X; G)/n admits a limit in the constant degree regime. This is proved in [AM15] for two symmetric disassortative communities, but the assortative case remains open. A recent result from [CKPZ16] further gives the expression for the limit in the disassortative case, but the assortative case remains open. [Notation of the source: (X, G) drawn from SSBM(n, 2, a/n, b/n), the symmetric two-community sparse stochastic block model; assortative means a > b; SNR = (a - b)^2/(2(a + b)).]
status_search: The specific open item (existence, and formula, of lim I(X;G)/n for the sparse assortative two-community SBM) is resolved. Abbe, Cornacchia, Gu, Polyanskiy, 'Stochastic block model entropy and broadcasting on trees with survey' (arXiv 2101.12601, 2021), abstract read verbatim: 'The limit of the entropy in the stochastic block model (SBM) has been characterized in the sparse regime for the special case of disassortative communities [COKPZ17] and for the classical case of assortative communities but in the dense regime [DAM16]. The problem has not been closed in the classical sparse and assortative case. This paper establishes the result in this case for any SNR besides for the interval (1, 3.513). It further gives an approximation to the limit in this window. The result is obtained by expressing the global SBM entropy as an integral of local tree entropies in a broadcasting on tree model with erasure side-information.' The remaining window is closed by Yu, Polyanskiy, 'Ising model on locally tree-like graphs: uniqueness of solutions to cavity equations' (arXiv 2211.15242, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 2024), abstract read verbatim: 'Our result simultaneously closes the following 6 conjectures in the literature: ... 6) characterization of entropy (and mutual information) of community labels given the graph in 2-SBM (ibid)' where 'ibid' is Abbe-Cornacchia-Gu-Polyanskiy'21. The broader first sentence of the bullet ('fundamental tradeoff ... for arbitrary constant degrees', k communities) is a research direction rather than a statement and is not what this row records; E0054 (Bandeira) already carries the k >= 3 weak-recovery threshold.
resolved_by: Abbe-Cornacchia-Gu-Polyanskiy, arXiv 2101.12601 (2021): the sparse assortative two-community SBM entropy limit 'for any SNR besides for the interval (1, 3.513)'; Yu-Polyanskiy, IEEE Trans. IT 2024 (arXiv 2211.15242): closes 'characterization of entropy (and mutual information) of community labels given the graph in 2-SBM' conjectured in the former. Together: I(X;G)/n admits a limit, with an explicit tree-based formula, for the assortative case at every SNR, which is the item the source calls open.
